hero.lead: A Himalayan nation of 29.6 million where citizens abroad send home a third of the economy, rivers give 84% of the power, and the World Bank approved $145 million for finance and digital services in February 2026.

capital.heading: Remittances, rivers and forests that earn.

record.text: Remittances received from citizens abroad, share of GDP, 2025
Paid for verified forest carbon reductions under the Forest Carbon Partnership Facility, November 2025
Total public debt at the end of Bhadra 2083 (mid-September 2026), 45.05% of GDP: Rs 1.611 trillion external and Rs 1.361 trillion domestic, from Public Debt Management Office figures

register.name: Extended Credit Facility (seventh and final review)
register.detail: IMF · Approved 12 January 2022 · Seventh and final review 8 June 2026 · Extended to 11 July 2026
register.note: SDR 282.42 million disbursed in total for budget support
register.text: The IMF’s 38-month Extended Credit Facility closed with its seventh and final review on 8 June 2026, which released SDR 31.32 million (about $42.9 million) and brought total disbursements for budget support to SDR 282.42 million. It is budget-wide support, not tied to one of the seven standards.

register.name: Greater Lumbini Area Development Project
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 13 March 2026 · P512377
register.note: Listed on the World Bank’s country finance page for Nepal; components not yet published
register.text: World Bank financing for the development of the Greater Lumbini area, around the birthplace of the Buddha. The World Bank’s country finance page lists the project without its components, so the standards it serves are not yet stated.

register.name: Clean Air and Prosperity Project
register.detail: World Bank · Approved March 2026 · $52 million credit and a $5 million grant
register.note: Plus a $5 million Resilient Asia Program grant (UK and Switzerland)
register.text: Cuts fine-particle (PM2.5) pollution from industrial and commercial boilers and furnaces in the Kathmandu Valley, the Terai and the surrounding foothills, helping about 400 enterprises adopt electric or modern biomass boilers and furnaces or advanced emission controls, and strengthens national air quality management. It serves health and energy.

register.name: Digital transformation
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Approved 9 February 2026 · Lead lender, with $40 million from ADB
register.text: Builds an integrated citizen service portal, an integrated social registry, a secure government-wide data exchange and a digital locker for verifiable credentials, and digitizes land administration. It serves livelihood by making public services and the social registry easier to reach.

register.name: Sustainable and inclusive finance
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 3 February 2026 · Sustainable and Inclusive Finance Project
register.text: Strengthens Nepal’s Deposit and Credit Guarantee Fund to share more of lenders’ risk and add guarantee products for underserved borrowers such as women-led businesses, and upgrades the technology and reach of the Credit Information Bureau of Nepal. It serves livelihood through credit for small firms and households.
register.note: Risk-sharing for lenders and a stronger credit bureau

register.name: Glacial lake outburst flood protection (FP272)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · Approved 3 July 2025 · Funded Activity Agreement 28 November 2025 · UNDP
register.note: Grant of $36,158,230, with $13.8 million of co-financing
register.text: Protects communities, infrastructure and ecosystems in Nepal’s glacial river basins from glacial lake outburst floods, combining the physical lowering of dangerous lakes with other measures, for 385,956 direct and 1,986,980 indirect beneficiaries. It serves shelter and livelihood in the mountains.

register.name: Second Green, Resilient and Inclusive Development Policy Credit
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 12 December 2024
register.text: Budget support for green and inclusive reform.

register.name: Disaster Resilience DPC with a Cat DDO
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 8 October 2024
register.text: Budget support that pays out when disaster strikes.

register.name: Provincial and Local Roads Improvement Program, Phase 1
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 29 February 2024
register.text: Roads for provinces and towns.

register.name: Strategic highways and wildlife conservation
register.detail: ADB · Announced 9 October 2026
register.text: Asian Development Bank financing to upgrade strategic highways and strengthen wildlife conservation in Nepal. It serves livelihood through the roads that carry trade and visitors.

register.name: Emergency response to the 2026 Bhotekoshi flood
register.detail: ADB · 28 August 2026 · Project 10014858-000
register.text: An immediate Asian Development Bank grant for the emergency response to the 2026 Bhotekoshi flood disaster. It is humanitarian relief, not tied to one of the seven standards.

register.name: SASEC Customs and Logistics Reforms Program, Subprogram 2
register.detail: ADB · Announced 1 July 2026 · Policy-based loan · Signed in July 2026
register.text: Supports customs digitalization, risk-based inspections and simpler procedures, and the planning, rules and coordination of logistics, to lower trade costs and make borders more predictable. It is budget-wide support for reform; it serves livelihood through trade and jobs.

register.name: Integrated Water Supply and Sewerage Management (Sector) Project
register.detail: ADB · Approved 18 June 2026 · Signed 6 July 2026 · Loan 4788-NEP, concessional
register.note: Water supply in eight towns, sanitation in seven
register.text: Brings water supply to Damak, Itahari, Birgunj, Butwal, Kohalpur-Karkado, Gurbhakot, Bhimdatta and Kerabari, and sanitation to Birgunj, Hetauda, Pokhara, Butwal, Nepalgunj, Bharatpur and Dhangadhi; ADB expects it to serve more than 850,000 people. It serves water, the standard furthest from reach, and shelter through sanitation.

register.name: Nepal Digital Transformation Project (ADB cofinancing)
register.detail: ADB · Announced 10 March 2026 · Concessional loan · ADB and World Bank Full Mutual Reliance Framework
register.note: The first project in South Asia under the framework; World Bank leads
register.text: ADB’s share of the digital transformation project led by the World Bank: government data hosting and cybersecurity, core digital public infrastructure, a citizen service portal, an improved national social registry and about 11 high-impact services digitized. It serves livelihood by making public services easier to reach.

register.name: Siddhartha Highway (Butwal–Pokhara) project preparation
register.detail: AIIB · Approved 22 September 2025 · Project Preparation Special Fund grant
register.note: Detailed project report and environmental and social assessments
register.text: Prepares the upgrade of the Butwal–Pokhara section of the Siddhartha Highway to modern standards, with realignment, widening, tunnels, viaducts, bridges and slope stabilization, to improve road safety, climate resilience and transport efficiency. It serves livelihood.

register.name: Air traffic control facilities at Tribhuvan International Airport
register.detail: JICA · Grant Agreement, 8 October 2026 · Completion expected in 2030
register.note: JPY 2,853 million grant, with an Exchange of Notes
register.text: Builds new air traffic control facilities, installs advanced air traffic management systems and supplies aviation equipment at the nation’s main international airport. It serves livelihood through the visitors and trade the airport carries.

register.name: Nagdhunga Tunnel Construction Project (II)
register.detail: JICA · Signed 3 June 2026 · 1.95% a year · 30 years, 10 years’ grace
register.note: Additional ODA loan; JICA loans for the tunnel now exceed ¥22 billion
register.text: Additional Japanese ODA loan for the 2.68 km Nagdhunga Tunnel, about 99% complete at signing, which improves the road link between Kathmandu and the rest of Nepal. It serves livelihood.

register.name: MCC Nepal Compact
register.detail: MCC · Signed 14 September 2017 · In force 30 August 2023 · Projects due by 30 August 2028
register.text: A United States grant for the Electricity Transmission Project, about 300 km of high-voltage lines and three substations, and the Road Maintenance Project; Nepal’s $197 million is the largest up-front partner contribution in MCC’s history. It serves energy and livelihood.

register.name: NMB Bank green bond
register.detail: IFC · April 2025 · Nepal’s first green bond · With BII and MetLife
register.note: IFC’s largest local currency investment in Nepal
register.text: Nepal’s first green bond and first thematic bond, issued by NMB Bank and anchored by IFC with British International Investment and MetLife, to finance small and medium enterprises in sustainable projects, including solar power and electric vehicles; it is projected to create about 8,000 jobs over five years. It serves energy and livelihood.

register.name: Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower (216 MW)
register.detail: AIIB approved 21 May 2019 · First disbursement October 2022 · MIGA exposure $87.4 million at 31 October 2026
register.note: Total cost; AIIB and IFC loans of up to $90 million each
register.text: A 216 MW run-of-river hydropower plant on the Upper Trishuli river, which IFC describes as of strategic national importance and the largest foreign direct investment in Nepal, co-financed by AIIB, IFC and ADB, with a MIGA guarantee. It serves energy.

register.name: Forest carbon credits
register.detail: Forest Carbon Partnership Facility · November 2025
register.text: Payment for verified emission reductions from Nepal’s community forests.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Diaspora
items.label: Of GDP sent home by citizens abroad, 2025
items.text: Nepalis working abroad send home a third of the economy.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Himalayan rivers give 84% of the power, with far more still to build and sell.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Community forests across more than two fifths of the land, already paid for the carbon they store.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Of export earnings from visitors, 2020
items.text: Everest, the Himalaya and Lumbini: visitors from every continent.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 28.1% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Gham Power
items.text: Solar irrigation pumps, farm data and advice for smallholders in the Terai, paid for with collateral-free loans from partner microfinance institutions; in its pilots farmers raised their incomes by up to 80%.

items.name: SmartPaani
items.text: A Kathmandu social enterprise for rainwater harvesting, filtration, recycling and wastewater treatment; with Dopper it has fitted 104 schools across Nepal with a safe water supply.

items.name: Diyalo Technologies
items.text: Billing, accounting and website services for drinking water consumer committees, 852 of them in March 2026, which GSMA reports serve about 1.2 million households.

items.name: Build Up Nepal
items.text: Trains and equips local entrepreneurs to make low-carbon interlocking earth bricks and build disaster-resilient homes: 12,000 houses built and about 220 active enterprises across Nepal.

items.name: Chhaya Nepal
items.text: Live video consultations, with the Karnali Province Ministry of Social Development, that link hospitals and health posts in Mugu, Humla, Dolpa, Jajarkot and Kalikot with specialists in Surkhet: 1,407 patients treated since April 2025.

coverage.gap_text: Of Nepalis lack safely managed drinking water.

guarantees.name: Shelter

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: About 372 kWh of electricity a person a year, against the Living Line of 1,000; 45% cook with clean fuels (2024)

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: 98.2% of young people complete lower secondary school

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: Above the national poverty line; 20.3% live below it
